turns.question: Where is middleware composition implemented?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the hono repo structure remotely using gh CLI.`compose.ts` looks like the key file. Let me read it.Now let's see how `compose` is invoked from `hono-base.ts`, which builds the middleware array.## Middleware composition in `honojs/hono`

**Core implementation: `src/compose.ts`** — exported function `compose()`

- Signature: `compose<E>(middleware, onError?, onNotFound?) => (context, next?) => Promise<Context>`
- It's an explicit port of the `koa-compose` pattern (stated in the file's own doc comment: *"Compose middleware functions into a single function based on `koa-compose` package"*).
- Internally it builds a recursive `dispatch(i)` closure:
  - Tracks a monotonically increasing `index` and throws `'next() called multiple times'` if `dispatch` is called out of order (i.e. `next()` invoked twice by a middleware).
  - Pulls `handler = middleware[i][0][0]` for the current position, or falls back to the `next` passed into the outer closure once `i === middleware.length` (this is how nested/child router composition chains into the parent's `next`).
  - Invokes `handler(context, () => dispatch(i + 1))`, i.e. each middleware receives a `next` that resumes the chain at `i+1` — the classic onion-model / continuation-passing composition.
  - Wraps the call in try/catch: on error, if `onError` is provided, it delegates to it and marks `isError = true`; otherwise rethrows.
  - If no handler exists at the end and `context.finalized === false`, it calls `onNotFound`.
  - Sets `context.res = res` when appropriate and returns the `context`.

**Where `compose` is invoked: `src/hono-base.ts`** (class `Hono`, exported as `HonoBase`)

- `#dispatch(request, executionCtx, env, method)`:
  - Matches routes via `this.router.match(method, path)`, producing `matchResult`.
  - **Fast path optimization**: if `matchResult[0].length === 1` (only one handler matched — no middleware stacked), it calls that single handler directly and skips `compose()` entirely (comment: `// Do not \`compose\` if it has only one handler`).
  - Otherwise: `const composed = compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` — builds the composed chain from all matched handlers (middleware + route handler(s), in router-match order) — then awaits `composed(c)` and returns `context.res`, throwing if the context wasn't finalized (no `Response` returned/`next()` awaited).
- `route()` method (sub-app mounting via `app.route(path, subApp)`): when the sub-app has a custom `errorHandler`, it wraps each sub-route handler using `compose([], app.errorHandler)(c, () => r.handler(c, next))` — i.e., an empty middleware array composed solely to get per-sub-app error handling around the route's own handler.
- `this.use = (...)` registers middleware handlers into the router (`#addRoute(METHOD_NAME_ALL, path, handler)`), so at request time the router returns the matched middleware + handler array in the right order, which `#dispatch` feeds into `compose`.

**Supporting evidence checked:**
- `src/compose.test.ts` exists alongside `compose.ts` (unit tests for the composition behavior) — I did not open it, so I haven't verified its exact test cases, only confirmed its presence.
- `COMPOSED_HANDLER` constant from `src/utils/constants` is used to tag route-grouped handlers that wrap a `compose()` call, letting the router/other code detect a composed handler and unwrap the original (`route()` method above).

**What I did not verify:**
- Contents of `src/compose.test.ts` (didn't read it, only confirmed it exists via directory listing).
- Router implementations (`src/router/*`) that produce `matchResult` — I didn't inspect `RegExpRouter`/`TrieRouter`/`LinearRouter` internals, only that `router.match()` returns the `[handler, route][]` array consumed by `compose`.
- Whether any other entry points (e.g. `hono/quick`, adapters in `src/adapter/*`) call `compose` differently — I only traced the main `Hono`/`HonoBase` class in `hono-base.ts`.
- Git history/blame of `compose.ts` for when/why it diverged from vanilla `koa-compose` (e.g., the not-found/error-handler additions) — not checked, just read current file content via `gh api`.

**Files/symbols to cite:**
- `src/compose.ts` — `compose()` function, inner `dispatch()`
- `src/hono-base.ts` — `Hono` class, `#dispatch()`, `use`, `route()`, `#addRoute()`

 * @property res - Optional response object to use.
 * @property message - Optional custom error message.
 * @property cause - Optional cause of the error.
 */
type HTTPExceptionOptions = {
  res?: Response
  message?: string
  cause?: unknown
}

/**
 * `HTTPException` must be used when a fatal error such as authentication failure occurs.
 *
 * @see {@link https://hono.dev/docs/api/exception}
 *
 * @param {StatusCode} status - status code of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions} options - options of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions["res"]} options.res - response of options of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions["message"]} options.message - message of options of HTTPException
 * @param {HTTPExceptionOptions["cause"]} options.cause - cause of options of HTTPException
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * import { HTTPException } from 'hono/http-exception'
 *
 * // ...
 *
 * app.post('/auth', async (c, next) => {
 *   // authentication
 *   if (authorized === false) {
 *     throw new HTTPException(401, { message: 'Custom error message' })
 *   }
 *   await next()
 * })
 * ```
 */
export class HTTPException extends Error {
  readonly res?: Response
  readonly status: ContentfulStatusCode

  constructor(status: ContentfulStatusCode = 500, options?: HTTPExceptionOptions) {

    this.res = options?.res
    this.status = status

   * Returns the response object associated with the exception.

  getResponse(): R
